chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Durust al-Wasiti, from 'Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'A woman performing Tamattu' arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menses). He said: She performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf with the House (Kaaba). If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tashriq (13th of Dhul-Hijjah), water is poured over her, and she pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj from her house and goes out to Mina, and completes all the rituals. When she returns to Mecca, she performs two Tawafs and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. When she does that, everything becomes permissible for her except the marital bed of her husband.'

key_terms.أَهَلَّتْ بِالْحَجِّ: She pronounced the Talbiyah for Hajj
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.مُتَمِّعَةٌ: A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّوْرِيَةِ: The Day of Tashriq (13th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman performing Tamattu' Hajj who is still menstruating upon arriving in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār clarifies the ruling for a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who arrives in Mecca while still menstruating, detailing her specific ritual adjustments. It establishes that she performs the initial Tawaf and Sa'i, then waits for purity or the Day of Tashriq to complete her Hajj rites, remaining in a state of Ihram restrictions until all are fulfilled. Scholarly tradition highlights this as a practical application of delaying the completion of Umrah until purity is achieved, ensuring the validity of the Tamattu' structure.
